item: Lost work and wages of evacuated workers
unit_cost: SEPH average weekly earnings 1204.92 / 5 per workday (nominal 2023)
method: evacuees x employed persons per resident (LFS employment 15+ / July 1 population) x days away x 5/7 workdays x daily earnings; First Nations on-reserve evacuees get 0.636 of the employment ratio (2021 Census on-reserve vs non-Indigenous employment rate) in low and central
source_name: Natural Resources Canada, Canadian Wildland Fire Evacuation Database (CWFEDB) Summary Stats 1980-2025, v2026-02-03; StatCan 14-10-0204-01 (SEPH annual AWE incl. overtime, all employees), 14-10-0223-01 (monthly), 14-10-0327-01 (LFS), 17-10-0005-01 (population); Christianson et al. 2024 IJWF 33 WF23097 (CWFEDB: 7.2 M person-days for 576,747 evacuees = 12.5 days; median event 7 days); ESDC QP note EF_063_20260105; ISC; StatCan 41-20-0002 (2023)
overlaps_with: econ_costs.csv GDP-loss and production rows (oil and gas shut-ins AB 2023 and 2025, accommodation, rail, iron ore, forestry): their value includes wages of the same evacuated workers, so count those wages once; EI benefits, NWT Evacuee Income Disruption Support, Nova Scotia Emergency Relief Grant and the EI pilot replace part of this income (transfers; not added). Alberta and Saskatchewan evacuation payments are for living costs and do not overlap.
notes: Evacuees: CWFEDB. Low case treats 27.5% as First Nations on reserve (long-run CWFEDB share; ISC publishes no 2023 count). Gross loss of work time, whoever bears it (worker or employer). Ignores remote work and paid leave (overstates) and self-employed income, workers outside evacuation zones whose workplaces closed, and smoke-related absences (understate).
